{{Article header|deck=Mining turns asteroid resources into refined cargo through method-specific extraction, collection, refining, and market planning.}}

'''Mining''' is the ship-based activity of extracting minerals, metals, and other commodities from asteroids, refining them into cargo, and selling them through commodity markets in ''Elite Dangerous''. This hub separates durable mining knowledge — methods, equipment, locations, and procedure flow — from time-sensitive information such as current best prices or high-demand sell stations.

== Start here ==

A mining run usually has five parts:

# choose a mining method and fit the ship for that method;
# bring enough limpets and cargo space for the planned run;
# travel to a suitable [[Planetary Rings|planetary ring]], hotspot, or known mining location;
# prospect, extract, collect, and refine the desired resources; and
# check current market data before selling the cargo.

New commanders should begin with [[How to Start Mining]]. Commanders who already understand the loop can use the method, equipment, and procedure tables below to jump to the relevant reference page.

== Equipment map ==

{{#invoke:Mining|equipmentTable}}

A mining ship normally carries an extraction tool, collector support, a refinery, cargo space, and enough limpets for the planned run. The exact layout depends on the method: a laser miner does not need seismic charges, while a core miner generally does not need to spend hardpoints on mining lasers.

== Locations and search concepts ==

{{#invoke:Mining|locationConcepts}}

Most ship-based mining happens in [[Planetary Rings|planetary rings]]. Ring hotspots revealed by a [[Detailed Surface Scanner]] are a planning aid rather than a guarantee; a commander still has to prospect individual asteroids and verify the current market before treating a run as profitable.

== Commodity planning ==

Mined commodities are useful only after they become cargo and reach a market with demand. EDFM should avoid hard-coding a permanent "best" commodity or station on this page: hotspots, routes, background simulation state, carrier markets, demand, and third-party data freshness all affect the practical answer.

{{#invoke:Mining|commodityConcepts}}
